claim: R4-08's rule at §4.11 *The clock* (4) (l.8446-8452) sends a calamity dated at or before the last epoch's week `W₀` to 'the first epoch folded by the absorb that carries it (… with none, the port folds one at the absorb's week for it), its `EpochInputs.events` entry at that epoch's first week (the last epoch's week + 1)', and folds no epoch only 'with the absorb's week itself before the last epoch's'. At `W₁` = `W₀` that has no possible outcome: an epoch at `W₀` on top of the last one, `years` 0, its event at `W₀` + 1 outside `(W₀, W₀]` (l.8325). V08's repair made the degenerate branch 'with `W₁` not after `W₀` (a clock turned back, or no week past the last epoch's)' — no epoch, 'its dated changes applied finished, noted' by the `late` variant (V08 §3.6 (3) l.1857-1864, §3.17 row l.2674, l.2933, T-V8-49 (g)); VPC-R4-02 asks the base to read so. But `W₁` = `W₀` is no clock turned back: it is any second absorb in the week of the last epoch, which follows whenever the previous sync's epoch fell at the dossier's present week (a calamity epoch at its own week, a year end, a crossing 'with none, at `W₁`'). A DM records a fire at week P, the map syncs (an epoch at P), then records a second calamity in the same week: it is dated `W₀`, carried late, and under V08 (and the base once VPC-R4-02 is applied as written) folds no epoch now or ever (it is no longer newly carried). Its hazard never strikes (DR28; V06 §3.11) and its deaths never reach the burial need (`CalamityRef.deaths`, V06 §3.18.2) — the loss R4-08 exists to prevent ('so its hazard strikes and its deaths reach the burial need'; item 122 (a)'s path 'the calamity … into the next epoch, V06's hazard phase'); recorded before one sync, both calamities would strike. The same absorb's population move is undefined too: V08 §3.6 (3)'s crossing epoch 'at the first week the population leaves … (with none, at `W₁` …)', 'every crossing inside the span', reads at `W₁` = `W₀` either as an epoch at `W₀` with `years` 0 (VPC-R4-02's own scenario) — whose late calamity then has an impossible event — or as none (the span `(W₀, W₀]` empty); V08's degenerate row names only `W₁ < W₀`. Two builders, two behaviours, and the defined one loses a calamity on a reachable path.
required_change: One fix with VPC-R4-02 (same sentence). (1) §4.11 *The clock* (4): 'with the absorb's week itself before the last epoch's (V08 §3.6's degenerate row) it folds no epoch and its dated changes apply finished, noted' → 'an absorb whose week is the last epoch's own (`W₁` = `W₀`: a second absorb before the dossier's clock moves) folds no epoch — a population move it carries crosses at the next absorb whose week passes `W₀`, and a calamity it newly carries applies its F5 targets' dossier events now as element events (finished, no Works) and rides, with its `EpochInputs.events` entry and its deaths, the first epoch a later absorb folds, at that epoch's first week, held meanwhile in the binding (`DossierBinding.lateCalamities`, V08 §2.3); only with the absorb's week before the last epoch's (a clock turned back; V08 §3.17's row for V08 §3.6) do its dated changes apply finished, noted (`unreceipted_change`'s `late` variant, V08 §4.6)'. (2) END under V08: §3.6 (3)'s '(with `W₁` not after `W₀`, V08 §3.17's degenerate row)' → '(with `W₁` = `W₀`, held in `DossierBinding.lateCalamities` for the first epoch a later absorb folds; with `W₁` before `W₀`, V08 §3.17's degenerate row)', and its crossing clause adds '— none when `W₁` = `W₀`, the crossing then read at the next absorb whose week passes `W₀`'; §2.3's `DossierBinding` gains `lateCalamities: CalamityRef[]` with its §2.6 lifecycle row (written by the ledger event of an absorb at `W₁` = `W₀` that newly carries a calamity; read and emptied by the next absorb that folds an epoch, each entry at that epoch's first week; persisted with the binding; no undo — an absorb is no undo target; absent in an older document `[]`); §3.17's row splits its 'with `W₁` not after `W₀`' clause the same way; the `late` variant's row (l.2933) 'by an absorb whose week is not after it' → 'by an absorb whose week is before it'; T-V8-49 (g) adds 'a second absorb in the last epoch's own week carrying a calamity dated that week and a population move past the tolerance — no epoch, the calamity's targets applied; then the next absorb past `W₀` folding the crossing and the calamity's strike at its first epoch's first week, its deaths in that epoch's burial need'. (3) END under scope: T76-1's late-calamity fixture adds 'and one carried by a second absorb in the last epoch's own week, held to the next absorb's first epoch'. (If the adjudicator rules the loss acceptable instead, VPC-R4-02's text applies as written, and V08 §3.17's row must still name the population move at `W₁` = `W₀` — no epoch — and the `late` variant's wording a same-week change.)

claim: §4.11's `wallToWay(enceinte)` (l. 8189–8196), the operator's home for epochs and hand converts alike, ends 'towers are removed; gates become junctions with a `square` option'. V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1605–1612; J-V6.114, J-V6.140) says '`absorbWall` and `wallToWay` leave standing every raised way that crosses the old line; the new ring road takes no junction with it: its opening or raised gate in the old curtain stays as a free-standing arch or gate tower'. §4.8 (l. 7643–7650) makes that raised gate 'a gate whose tower carries the deck'. A builder of §4.11's operator removes the tower that carries a standing viaduct's deck and makes its gate a junction; the evolution builder keeps both. Two units state two outcomes for one case (R3-03 (b)), and §4.11's reading leaves a deck without its support.
required_change: §4.11 *`wallToWay(enceinte)`*: 'towers are removed; gates become junctions with a `square` option.' → 'towers are removed; gates become junctions with a `square` option — save the stretch held under a raised way's crossing station while its deck stands (a raised gate with its tower, the curtain under an aqueduct's arch), which stays as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, the new ring road taking no junction with the raised way (§2.7's support step (3); V06 §3.7.6 (5)).'

claim: §4.3 *Lattice and costs* (l. 5629-5632) gives the generation regime 'At generation, before the span rule has run' (a later stage's way crosses an unlocked raised way's strip wherever the soffit clears), but §2.7's support step (6) (a) (l. 2577) runs the span rule on an S4 or S5b viaduct at a stage's S5a commit ('re-run (1)–(5), and then the span rule, on it in the same commit'), before that stage's S5c grows. claim: In §4.11 *The clock* (4) (l. 8447–8451), a calamity carried late rides the absorb's first epoch: 'with none, the port folds one at the absorb's week for it', and 'with the absorb's week itself before the last epoch's (V08 §3.6's degenerate row) it folds no epoch'.
